text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- China's top leaders hold private farewell ceremony for country's economic architect Deng Xiaoping before remains cremated.
- Singapore soccer star Fandi Ahmad will retire from international soccer after Southeast Asian Games in Jakarta in Octobr if he is asked to continue playing as striker.
- Eight departments under Home Affairs Ministry will train and work more closely to achieve world-class standard of safety and security for Singapore under its Home Team concept.

- Indonesia's environment minister describes talk of a nuclear power plant in country as premature as yet another local non-government organisation attacks nuclear energy bill due to be passed by parliament.
- Three-pronged strategy unveiled by Trade Development Board to develop Singapore into a global city of international trade.
- Foreign tranches of five Morgan Stanley Capital International stocks sold down on concern they will be affected by proposed changes to benchmark index.
- Urban Redevelopment Authority grants provisional permission for several residential projects, paving way for work to begin on some of them in next 12 months.
- Creative Technology shares fall as much as 13 percent before recovering to close 7.5 percent lower following news of Cyrix Corp's new media microprocessor.
- Property consultants give mixed views on proposal by National Development Minister Lim Hng Kiang to move railway station at Tanjong Pagar to another site within city.
- Property companies expected to post modest earnings growth of 15-20 percent for 1996, with mid-sized developers such as DBS Land, Straits Steamship Land and Malayan Credit among better performers.
- Property stocks tumble after government makes clear it will not withdraw or ease measures announced last May to curb property speculation.
- Logistics infrastructure group Eng Kong Holdings says it receives in-principle approval to list shares on SESDAQ, Singapore's second board.
